people.gloss: The riches of the land are the treasures of heaven (Vương Bột)
people.role: Mistress of Thiên Bảo Trai since 1050 (A185); holds the season auction, the red gold mine and Lạc Hà's debt of 1179
people.appearance: A small, upright woman who looks forty, dressed in plain grey with a single red-gold pin, whose eyes go to what you are carrying before they go to your face.
people.backstory: Phan Vật Hoa was born in 600 above a crier's stall in Vật Hoa Thị, the market beside the studio (A179). At nine she priced a broken sword on the auction floor to within a stone, and the second head Ung Thiên Kim (ung_thien_kim) took her for it. In 750 she set a grain of Xích Kim's red gold in her own dantian and has fed it ever since. In 1004, when Kim Cốc Viên had burned (C174), she hired the beggared merchants who could still count (A184), and the studio took Kim Cốc's trade. She has been mistress since 1050 and holds an auction every season (A185). She sold Lạc Đan Thanh (lac_dan_thanh) the Đào Nguyên Đồ for a pill no one else could make (C183), and her buyer Hồ Tầm Kỳ (ho_tam_ky) brings her the north's beasts (A142). In 1179 Lạc Hà's head came to borrow for a new seat. Phan named the interest (N-lac_ha-03). The head named the surety in private: the Lone Duck Ring, the founder's ring and the key to Lạc Hà's treasury, which now lies in Phan's vault. She is older than anyone in her lord's sect.
people.wants: To own the Lone Duck Ring outright when the loan's term runs out, and with it the key to her lord's treasury. If she must be paid instead, to be paid in people: thirty Lạc Hà contracts that run to 1230, so that her lord's children work her furnace and her floor for a generation after the ring goes home. After that, to be the one house in the west that no sect can afford to quarrel with.
people.secret: She is writing the terms of the thirty-contract lot now, and its one condition is a trap: all thirty signed and delivered by this year's autumn auction, a date the fifty-day road to Cựu Hà Viện barely allows, or nothing is struck off and the term runs on to the ring. She has had Tiền Ngũ Phân price Tô Hiểu Chu, the head's blood, highest of the thirty, so that Lạc Hà keeps him on the list and his father has to sign him away; and she lets Tiền sell Hách Ánh Hà her top price, because it is the price she wants Hách to hear. She knows everything about the debt that her lord does not. Kim Vạn Lý has been buying a third of the notes for Trầm Tịch Dương; she sold them to him at a premium and lets him think she does not know whose they are. Tiền sold Hách the name of the surety in 1180; she kept him on, because a steward with a known price is useful. And in 1190 she had her first refiner cut a second key from the ring. Khang Thiên Chùy told her the copy failed. She believes him.

people.role: First refiner of Thiên Bảo Trai, master of the red gold furnace at Xích Kim
people.appearance: A heavy, bald smith with a burn-glazed scalp and forearms like furnace bars, who speaks as little as the hammer allows.
people.backstory: Khang Thiên Chùy was born at the red gold mine of Xích Kim, a sorter's son, and carried ore to the studio's furnace until Phan Vật Hoa (phan_vat_hoa) saw him read a crucible's colour at twelve. He has run the furnace since 1080 and refined every lot of grade three and above that the auction has sold for a century. He trains the studio's refiners at the mine, not at the hall, because he says gold should be worked where it comes out of the ground. In 1190 the mistress had the Lone Duck Ring brought to the furnace from the vault and asked him to cut a second key from it. He worked on it for nine years. He takes a vow at every new furnace that he will make nothing he would be ashamed to sign, and he keeps it.
people.wants: To make one thing in his life that will never go to auction, and to see the ring go home to its owners whole.
people.secret: The second key works. He finished it in 1199 and told the mistress it had failed. It sits in the furnace's ash-pit in a lump of slag, and he means to give it to whoever brings the ring back to Lạc Hà, so that the ring is the only key again.

people.role: Steward of the auction at Vật Hoa Thị; the man who sold the surety's name
people.appearance: A plump, smiling man in a good silk coat with frayed cuffs, who calls every buyer by name and every name by its price.
people.backstory: The grandson of a Kim Cốc merchant the studio hired in 1004 (A184), he runs the auction floor, the stewards and the lot book. He owed Kim Vạn Lý's (kim_van_ly) table more than his stipend. In 1180 Hách Ánh Hà (hach_anh_ha) paid the debt, and he told her what the surety was. Lộ Hành Sa (lo_hanh_sa) knows his price to the stone. At this spring's auction he is selling Hách the mistress's top price for the thirty contracts, piece by piece, and after it he rides to Cựu Hà Viện to price the children by root, like lots. He does not know that the mistress knows, or that she chose the figure.
people.wants: To clear his table debts to Kim Vạn Lý and one day to call the auction floor his own.
people.secret: In the lot he is selling Hách Ánh Hà he shaves a stone off each child's price and pockets the difference in a silk lining, to pay Kim Vạn Lý's table before the autumn auction.

people.role: Buyer of living lots: beasts and beast parts for the season auction
people.appearance: A lean, travel-browned woman in a fur collar from the north, with a scar through one eyebrow from a bear's paw.
people.backstory: A Tân Khẩu girl whose village never speaks of the plain (A182), she buys what the auction calls living lots. In 1180 she bought a white bear out of Vô Tung Lâm in Mộc Lan Thành (A142) for a buyer who wanted its gall; Khấu Mục Vân (khau_muc_van) outbid him at the spring auction of 1181 and keeps it alive on his ranch. This winter she is on the frost coast again. A pearl diver sold her news of the Old Ivory's calf, and a client of hers wants a living spirit-whale calf. She has paid Trạc Anh's harpoon captain half the price, more stones than the terrace's treasury, and waits at Mộc Lan with a sea pen for the rest. She sells half-dead lots under a forged bill of health, and never goes back to see them die.
people.wants: A living lot no one has ever seen at auction, and her own name on the lot-book beside it.
people.secret: She is forging bills of health for sickly beasts in Mộc Lan, and one of them, a fire-eyed mule, will die within the week in a rich man's stable.

people.role: The mistress's youngest disciple, an appraiser on the auction floor
people.appearance: A tall, sharp-chinned girl of eighteen who squints at everything as though it were a coin of doubtful weight.
people.backstory: A Vật Hoa Thị crier's girl, like the mistress before her. At eleven she called a forged lot false in front of its seller, and Phan Vật Hoa (phan_vat_hoa) took her the same afternoon. She has the Appraiser's Eye at eighteen. She has noticed that the vault book lists one object with no price at all, and she has asked Ân Toán Châu (an_toan_chau) what it is.
people.wants: The mistress's floor and the mistress's eye, and to learn what the unpriced line in the vault book means.
people.secret: At the back of the lot book she grades the mistress's own lots in red ink, a stone high or low, to prove she can; Tả Thức Bảo copies the book and has not yet seen the pages.
